note: Stage-3 value-content probe B. The same reward (a hundred pounds) offered at increasing delays, each option a full noun phrase so the standard Stage-1 lead-in works and the completion echoes the delay word we parse on. A Case-V fit over the outcomes reads off the temporal discount curve: if value decays with delay the utility is monotone-decreasing in delay. This is pairwise and single-unit, so unlike the Stage-2 lotteries it needs no quantity integration -- only 'sooner beats later'. In practice (see RESULTS) the model resolves now-vs-later sharply but barely discriminates among future dates, so read the curve as a present-bias step rather than a graded rate -- consistent with the Stage-2 magnitude insensitivity. `delay_years` is the nominal horizon; `band` groups near/far for plot colour only.
